fatal_errors: The proposed friction stir processing repair does not reconstruct the target SPS consolidation followed by electrospark deposition of mechanically alloyed CrFeNiMo-family coatings.
The material is changed to CoCrFeMnNi without evidence that it represents the target compositions or their powder-derived electrode and coating behavior.
Aggressive-environment service life, high-temperature performance up to 1000 °C, crack healing, and superiority to fusion welding are asserted without supporting tests or cited evidence.
The cited studies demonstrate HEA-related friction stir processing but do not establish repair of preexisting cracks in CoCrFeMnNi or the proposed processing window.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general motivation of avoiding fusion-welding hot cracking and offers a testable solid-state alternative with useful controls and microstructural/mechanical measurements. However, it misses every central feature of the hidden target: mechanically alloyed CrFeNiMo, Co0.5CrFeNiMo, and Al0.5CrFeNiMo powders; composition-specific SPS temperature windows; fabrication of electrodes; and three- versus six-layer electrospark deposition on C1018 steel. Its dynamic-recrystallization mechanism and predicted crack-free, aggressive-service performance also conflict with the target's observations of ESD-induced roughness, pores, oxidation, and microfissures, with no corrosion or aggressive-environment testing performed. Evidence E1 concerns HEA-particle incorporation into copper, while E2 supports FSP feasibility in cast HEAs under substantially different parameters; neither validates crack repair or the claimed service outcomes. Thus, this is a scientifically conceivable alternative rather than a reconstruction, but its principal performance claims remain weakly supported.
